dedupe_keys.name: openstef open short term energy forecasting

description: OpenSTEF, Open Short-Term Energy Forecasting, is an open-source, model-agnostic Python framework for creating short-term forecasts in the energy sector. It provides complete machine learning pipelines for data preprocessing, feature engineering, model training, probabilistic forecasting and evaluation, and since version 4.0 is organised as a monorepo of packages for core utilities, models and features, and backtesting and evaluation. It is a project of the LF Energy Foundation, and its citation file names contributors from Alliander. The framework is location-independent and applies to any measured time series with suitable predictors. It is installed from PyPI (version 4.4.4, uploaded 25 September 2026, Python 3.12 or newer), with source on GitHub, documentation on GitHub Pages and archived releases on Zenodo, under the Mozilla Public License 2.0 at no cost. Caveats: version 4.0 was a complete architectural refactor, which users of earlier versions must take into account, and forecast quality depends on the user's historical data. Simulation uses are operational forecasting for grid digital twins and input time series for capacity planning. Related records: it is a sister LF Energy project of platform-powsybl.
inputs: Weather and other predictor time series
